Meta-analytic predictive prior of an event probability

Source: R/map_beta.R
map_beta.Rd

Derives the meta-analytic predictive (MAP) prior of the event probability per unit time in a new control arm from historical control arms with the hierarchical Beta model of Brock et al. (2023), and returns it as a mixture of Beta distributions for mapbern_post.

Usage

map_beta(
  events = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  t = NULL,
  study = NULL,
  a_prior = c(1/3, 1/3),
  b_prior = c(5, 5),
  tol = 1e-10,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

events

Numbers of subjects with the event in the historical arms (summary data with one unit of time at risk per subject).

n

Numbers of subjects in the historical arms (summary data).

y, t, study

Subject-level data instead of events and n: event indicators, times at risk, and arm identifiers.

a_prior

Shape parameters of the Beta prior of \(a\); the default is that of Brock et al. (2023).

b_prior

Shape parameters of the Beta prior of \(b\); the default is that of Brock et al. (2023).

tol

Total weight of the components that may be dropped.

control

List of settings of the numerical integration: n_coarse (default 41), n_ab (Gauss-Legendre nodes per coordinate, default 32), n_pi (nodes per panel for subject-level data, default 16), eps (default 1e-8), max_iter (default 12) and check (default TRUE).

Value

A data frame with columns w, shape1 and shape2, one row per component of the mixture, ordered by decreasing weight. Its attributes are n_total (\(N\)), hyper (posterior means of \(a\) and \(b\)), moments (mean and standard deviation of the MAP prior) and error (with control$check = TRUE, the largest absolute difference of the MAP prior distribution function at its 2.5, 50 and 97.5 percent points between the default and a finer grid).

Details

Historical arm \(j\) of \(J\) has \(N_j\) subjects, and \(N = \sum_j N_j\). With the event probability \(\pi_j\) per unit time and a constant hazard, a subject with time at risk \(t\) has the event with probability \(1 - (1 - \pi_j)^t\). The model is $$\pi_j \mid a, b \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a b N, (1 - a) b N), \quad a \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a_1, a_2), \quad b \sim \mathrm{Beta}(b_1, b_2),$$ so \(a\) is the mean event probability and \(b\) discounts the historical information. The MAP prior of the probability \(\pi^*\) in a new arm is $$p(\pi^*) = \int\int \mathrm{Beta}(\pi^*; a b N, (1 - a) b N) \, p(a, b \mid \mathrm{data}) \, da \, db.$$ The posterior of \((a, b)\) is integrated by Gauss-Legendre quadrature on \((\mathrm{logit}(a), \mathrm{logit}(b))\) after a coarse grid has located the region of the posterior mass; each quadrature node gives one Beta component of the mixture, with the quadrature weight times the posterior density as its weight. The components with the smallest weights, which together have a weight of at most tol, are dropped. Brock et al. (2023) sample the same model by MCMC and approximate the predictive distribution by a mixture fitted to the draws.

The likelihood of an arm is the Beta-binomial probability when only the numbers of events (events, n) are given, which assumes one unit of time at risk for every subject. With subject-level data (y, t, study), \(\pi_j\) is integrated out by Gauss-Legendre quadrature on \(\mathrm{logit}(\pi_j)\).

References

Brock, K., Chen, C., Ho, S., Fuller, G., Woolfolk, J., McShea, C. and Penard, N. (2023). A Bayesian method for safety signal detection in ongoing blinded randomised controlled trials. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 22(2), 378–395. doi:10.1002/pst.2278

See also

mapbern_post

Examples

prior <- map_beta(events = c(9, 11, 10), n = c(100, 100, 100))
attr(prior, "moments")
#>       mean         sd 
#> 0.10334757 0.03403532 
nrow(prior)
#> [1] 1422
